thNote.text:
Eight themes, one design

The layout is the Round 3 design you liked. Only the colours change.

The top two rows use our app's current colours, taken from frontend/src/index.css: dark (obsidian + indigo) and light.

Every Round 3 and Round 4 screen has a Theme setting: select a screen, open Tweaks, and pick Espresso, Obsidian, Daylight, Amethyst, Sapphire, Emerald, Burgundy or Ivory.

noteR4a.text:
Option 1 — Today list

No sidebar. Home is a short to-do list for today, with one button per item and a progress bar.

Approving opens a focus screen: one post at a time, two huge buttons, nothing else to look at.

Best for: busy owners who open the app for 5 minutes a day.

Press Play on Home and click Approve.

noteR4b.text:
Option 2 — Posts board

Every post is a card that moves left to right: Drafts → Waiting for OK → Scheduled → Posted. You can see where everything is at a glance, like a Trello board.

Click a card and its details open on the right, with Approve right there.

Best for: agencies and teams with many posts in flight.

noteR4c.text:
Option 3 — Big buttons

Home is four big buttons: Create, Approve, Calendar, Accounts. Each shows its count. Below, a plain-English timeline of what will happen next.

The same layout works on a phone with no changes.

Best for: first-time and non-technical users.

noteR3.text:
Clickable prototype

Press Play on Home, then click the sidebar, Review, New post or Calendar to move between pages.

Every page uses this one sidebar, so a change here shows everywhere.

Photos are stand-ins. Real post photos replace them in the app.

noteA.text:
Option A — Spotlight review

Closest to the reference. One post at a time, large and clear, with Approve and schedule always visible at the bottom of the card.

The right column answers "where will this go?" (only this brand's accounts, with a Reconnect button when one is broken) and "what else is happening this week?".

Best for: an owner who approves a few posts a day.

noteB.text:
Option B — Inbox

List on the left, the open post on the right, like email. Status tabs with counts, a brand filter that is always visible, and "Assigned to me".

Schedule, channels and reviewer sit beside the preview, so nothing is hidden below the fold.

Best for: agencies working through many posts across many brands.

noteC.text:
Option C — Calendar first

The week is the home screen. Approved posts with no date wait in "Ready to schedule" on the left.

New post and Edit open a drawer over the calendar, so you never lose your place. The drawer walks through Write, Photos, Where and When, and photos can be added before saving.

Best for: planning the month ahead.
